lede: Carolina had last change, so Rod Brind'Amour picked most of these matchups. Columbus played without Dmitri Voronkov.

notes.head: The fourth line drew Heinen’s line
notes.text: Rod Brind'Amour sent Robinson, Kotkaniemi and Deslauriers out for 5:45 of their 7:55 at 5-on-5 against Heinen, Del Bel Belluz and Lomberg (73%, about 16% with no line matching).

notes.head: The third line drew Knies’s line
notes.text: Martinook, Jankowski and Jarvis spent 11:05 of their 13:47 at 5-on-5 against Knies, Coyle and Olivier (80%, about 25% with no line matching), and the chances were close, 0.74 to 0.62 expected goals. Carolina scored two of its three goals then.

notes.head: Ehlers’s line drew Sillinger’s line
notes.text: Ehlers, Stankoven and Blake spent 10:07 of their 13:53 at 5-on-5 against Sillinger, Monahan and Garland (73%, about 26% with no line matching), and they had the better of the chances, 0.56 to 0.22 expected goals. Carolina scored one of its three goals then.

notes.head: One matchup went wrong
notes.text: Carrier, Aho and Svechnikov kept drawing Columbus’s first line, Nichushkin, Fantilli and Johnson. In those 11:25 Columbus had 0.69 expected goals to Carolina’s 0.10.

foot: Rod Brind'Amour matched about as hard as in his other home games: each line spent 76% of its time against one opposing line, against 47% to 78% in his first five.
